assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are, to me, the clearest case where lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour became a medicine: pH-dependent ionizable lipids, helper lipids and PEG-lipids co-assemble with nucleic acid into particles that encapsulate, protect and release cargo. The concept is original, physically grounded and has had very large impact through siRNA and mRNA vaccines.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Hope and Madden established the early lipid-based nucleic-acid encapsulation and ionizable-lipid approach; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipidoid discovery; MacLachlan contributed formulation translation. A three-person configuration is possible, but the split between the Vancouver lineage and the MIT lineage is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation at global scale and independent confirmation across multiple formulations and companies make this mature and timely.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the Vancouver and MIT/industry groups is unresolved.
Part of the prize-worthy chemistry may be seen as overlapping with the mRNA-vaccine work already recognized in Medicine 2023.
I am relying on recollection of the lipid design history rather than verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframe intracellular organization as a physical-chemical phase-separation problem driven by multivalent weak interactions, which is directly the thermodynamics and colloid chemistry I work with. The concept is new, general and has reshaped cell biology, though its status as chemistry rather than biology is debated.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated liquid-like P granules; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction framework in reconstituted systems; Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physical theory. Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen form a plausible trio, but the theorists' contributions complicate this.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing and widely replicated, but the physiological relevance of many reported condensates and the role of true phase separation versus other assembly mechanisms are still debated, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Controversy over which cellular assemblies are genuine liquid-liquid phase separation.
Boundary between chemistry and cell biology for prize purposes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages is a clean demonstration of thermodynamically controlled, error-correcting assembly giving defined architectures with host-guest function and confined catalysis. It established a general design concept for molecular organization.
assessment.attribution: Fujita, Raymond and Stang each independently developed coordination-driven discrete assemblies in the 1990s with distinct design logics; this makes a trio natural. Nitschke and Ward are important later contributors on complexity and function.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and broad adoption; recognition is timely and not premature, though it may be seen as overlapping with the 2016 and 1987 supramolecular prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier supramolecular Nobel Prizes.
Limited practical applications compared with other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami and programmable DNA nanostructures give a general, predictable route to arbitrary nanoscale organization using base-pairing thermodynamics and kinetics. Rothemund's folding scaffold paradigm is original and heavily used, building on the structural DNA nanotechnology of Seeman, whose absence from the list complicates the story.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund is the clear central figure for origami; Winfree contributed algorithmic self-assembly and the computational framing; Yan, Yin and Shih extended the field with tiles, bricks and 3D designs.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature field with extensive independent replication, but application impact beyond research tools is still emerging.
uncertainties: Seeman is not credited in the supplied names, creating an attribution gap for the founding concept.
Distance between concept and practical impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry brings intact non-covalent protein complexes, including membrane protein-lipid assemblies, into the gas phase and preserves stoichiometry and interactions. It opened a new way to study molecular assembly, which resonates with my interest in lipid-protein interactions.
assessment.attribution: Chait, Loo, Heck and Robinson each developed pieces; Robinson's membrane-protein and lipid work and Heck's complex analysis are particularly decisive, with Loo for early charge-state and complex studies.
assessment.maturity: Well established and reproduced widely, but part of it may be viewed as an extension of electrospray ionization already recognized in 2002.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 Nobel Prize for biomolecular mass spectrometry.
Whether gas-phase structures faithfully reflect solution structure in all cases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation, through PROTACs and molecular glues, introduces a new pharmacological concept: induced proximity to hijack ubiquitin ligases. It is conceptually original and has produced clinical candidates.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies pioneered PROTACs; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, underpinning molecular glues; Ciulli contributed structure-based design. A three-person split is plausible but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Clinical outcomes are still developing and approvals of degraders are limited, so recognition may be premature compared with more established candidates.
uncertainties: Separation of PROTAC and molecular glue contributions.
Part of the story is biology of the ubiquitin system, already recognized in 2004.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory of protein folding provides a general statistical-mechanical principle explaining how proteins avoid kinetic traps, linking thermodynamics to biological function. It is a deep physical-chemical concept that changed how folding is understood.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) developed the funnel landscape; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model perspective; Fersht provided experimental mapping. Credit is distributed and a clean trio is difficult.
assessment.maturity: The concept is mature and widely accepted, though its practical consequences were partly eclipsed by structure prediction recognized in 2024.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers and soft lithography established molecular control of interfaces and a simple, general approach to patterning surfaces, central to surface and colloid chemistry. The concept is original and has had a broad influence on materials and biointerface research.
assessment.attribution: Sagiv initiated organosilane monolayers; Nuzzo and Allara demonstrated thiols on gold; Whitesides greatly expanded and applied SAMs and soft lithography. Credit is spread across decades and several groups.
assessment.maturity: A mature field with extensive confirmation; its timeliness is long-standing, so it may be seen as less novel than recent candidates.
uncertainties: Complicated credit including Sagiv's early work.
Whether the impact is deemed sufficiently fundamental compared with the leading candidates.
